programme: HAND2, CREM and ATF5 each list TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme of catecholamine/dopamine biosynthesis) among their targets, converging on transcriptional control of the same node: HAND2 as the developmental specifier of the noradrenergic/catecholaminergic neural-crest lineage (also driving DBH, PHOX2B, GATA4 in its target set), CREM as the cAMP/PKA-responsive activator classically acting at the TH promoter, and ATF5 as a stress-responsive factor with the same target. EGR3, an activity-dependent immediate-early gene, sits downstream of the same catecholaminergic/neuronal-activity signaling.
role_in_a: In bladder cancer, HAND2 is a validated epigenetically-silenced gene used as a urine methylation biomarker (PMID 42211507, 39567591), consistent with loss of the differentiation program it would otherwise run. CREM and ATF5 have no bladder-cancer-specific literature in this record — only Open Targets percentile scores — so their role here, if any, is unconfirmed rather than documented.
role_in_b: TH transcriptional control is textbook-central to Parkinson's disease dopaminergic biology, and EGR3 was flagged as a candidate differential-expression biomarker in a PD gene-expression profiling study (PMID 23284986). But nothing in the record places HAND2, CREM or ATF5 specifically in PD — their relevance rests on general catecholamine-pathway knowledge, not on retrieved evidence.
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would be that both diseases perturb the transcriptional layer around TH/catecholamine genes: developmentally silenced in neoplastic urothelium (HAND2) versus dysregulated in stressed dopaminergic neurons (CREM/ATF5/EGR3). This bridges two very different cell contexts (neural-crest-lineage urothelium vs. midbrain dopaminergic neurons/peripheral blood) and is a mechanistic inference, not something documented for this pair.
reasoning: The module is nameable — three of the twelve concordant factors converge on TH, a biologically meaningful hub — and HAND2 is genuinely well-placed in bladder cancer while EGR3 is genuinely placed in PD. But the two placements never meet: HAND2's documented bladder role is as a silenced methylation marker, not as part of a catecholamine-synthesis story, and CREM/ATF5 have zero disease-specific evidence in either disease. The rest of the concordant set (HOXA13, PITX2, SOX5, SP7, ESRRA, KLF14, JARID2) belongs to a separate, better-documented axis — developmental/differentiation TFs silenced in urothelium — that has no counterpart in the PD literature retrieved, and I am deliberately not folding those into this programme.
support: PMID 42211507 — HAND2 urinary methylation biomarker for bladder cancer diagnosis. PMID 39567591 — HAND2 among novel urine methylation markers for bladder cancer detection. PMID 23284986 — EGR3 identified as a candidate biomarker in Parkinson's disease via gene-expression profiling/bioinformatics. No retrieved PMID connects HAND2, CREM, or ATF5 to Parkinson's disease, or connects any of the four carrying factors to catecholamine biology in bladder tissue.
how_to_falsify: Test HAND2, CREM and ATF5 occupancy at the TH locus by ChIP or reporter assay in a bladder-derived line and in a dopaminergic model (SH-SY5Y or iPSC-derived DA neurons); if TH expression is unchanged upon knockdown/knockout of these factors in either system, the shared TH target is a network/annotation artifact rather than a real regulatory module. Separately, attempt to replicate the EGR3 differential-expression finding in an independent PD cohort with matched controls and check correlation with TH or other dopaminergic markers.
caveats: Tissue pairing is bladder vs. blood — no CNS tissue is directly represented on the PD side. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 225 patient-group comparisons, so the large comparison count may reflect repeated subgroup splits within the same two cohorts rather than independent replication. HAND2, HOXA13, SOX5, PITX2, ESRRA and FOXF1 all have direct bladder-cancer literature support as differentiation/methylation-marker genes — that is a real, separate axis this account does not explain, and readers should not assume the TH-convergence story accounts for the whole concordant set. FOXF1 is discordant and was excluded as evidence rather than used to support the pairing.
